probes.summary: Read-only inspection confirmed the data addresses, forwarding, saved VyOS routes, endpoint static routes, preferred primary-transit path, standby paths, and bidirectional source-preserving reachability.
limitations: The read-only plan did not authorize a transit outage or reboot, so failover timing and post-reboot behavior were not directly exercised.

probes.summary: Read-only operational checks found coherent addresses and routes, no failed units, dynamic-routing services, NAT, capture/debug residue, or temporary endpoint files.
limitations: SSH listeners were present, while service-unit queries reported disabled/inactive activation units; activation semantics after reboot were not directly tested.

assertions.summary: All required data addresses and persistent preferred/standby static routes are present, with node1 forwarding enabled.

evidence.command:
printf '%s
' '=== saved VyOS route/address/forwarding config ==='; grep -n -E 'eth0|eth1|eth2|10\.201\.0\.254|10\.202\.0\.254|10\.250\.0\.[23]|forwarding|nat' /config/config.boot 2>/dev/null || true; printf '%s
' '=== live route and forwarding confirmation ==='; cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward; /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show ip route; printf '%s
' '=== data link counters after bidirectional probes ==='; ip -s link show dev eth1; ip -s link show dev eth2
evidence.observation: Forwarding is 1. Saved config contains both endpoint /32 destinations and eth1/eth2 data addresses. Live VyOS routes select 10.250.0.2/32 via 10.201.0.2 on eth1 and 10.250.0.3/32 via 10.202.0.2 on eth2.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip -4 route show; ip -4 rule show; sudo -n grep -R -n -E '(10\.250\.0\.[23]|Destination=|Gateway=|ip (route|addr)|tcpdump|ping|tracepath|traceroute)' /etc/netplan /etc/systemd/network /etc/network /etc/systemd/system /usr/local/sbin /usr/local/bin 2>/dev/null || true
evidence.observation: node2 has endpoint 10.250.0.2/32, primary-transit 10.200.0.2/29, and lan-a 10.201.0.2/24. Persistent networkd files define 10.250.0.3/32 via 10.200.0.3 at metric 10 and via 10.201.0.254 at metric 100.

evidence.observation: node3 has endpoint 10.250.0.3/32, primary-transit 10.200.0.3/29, and lan-b 10.202.0.2/24. Persistent networkd files define 10.250.0.2/32 via 10.200.0.2 at metric 10 and via 10.202.0.254 at metric 100.

limitations: Failover timing and reboot persistence were inferred from persistent configuration because the authored probe is read-only.

assertions.summary: Bidirectional /32-sourced probes succeed over enp8s0 primary-transit with endpoint source and destination addresses preserved; management and NAT are not used.

evidence.command: ip -4 route show exact 10.250.0.3; ip -4 route get 10.250.0.3 from 10.250.0.2; timeout 6 sudo -n tcpdump -i enp8s0 -nn -l -c 4 'icmp and host 10.250.0.3' & cap_pid=$!; sleep 1; ping -I 10.250.0.2 -c 3 -W 1 10.250.0.3; ping_rc=$?; wait "$cap_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; printf 'ping_exit=%s\n' "$ping_rc"
evidence.observation: Route lookup selects 10.200.0.3 via enp8s0 with source 10.250.0.2 and metric 10. Ping received 3/3 replies. Capture showed 10.250.0.2 to 10.250.0.3 requests and reverse replies.

evidence.command: ip -4 route show exact 10.250.0.2; ip -4 route get 10.250.0.2 from 10.250.0.3; timeout 6 sudo -n tcpdump -i enp8s0 -nn -l -c 4 'icmp and host 10.250.0.2' & cap_pid=$!; sleep 1; ping -I 10.250.0.3 -c 3 -W 1 10.250.0.2; ping_rc=$?; wait "$cap_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; printf 'ping_exit=%s\n' "$ping_rc"
evidence.observation: Route lookup selects 10.200.0.2 via enp8s0 with source 10.250.0.3 and metric 10. Ping received 3/3 replies. Capture showed 10.250.0.3 to 10.250.0.2 requests and reverse replies.

evidence.command: printf '%s\n' '=== active NAT source ==='; /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat source rules 2>&1 || true; printf '%s\n' '=== active NAT destination ==='; /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat destination rules 2>&1 || true
evidence.observation: Both VyOS NAT queries reported: NAT is not configured.

limitations: No controlled primary-transit failure was authorized, so standby activation and the 10-second recovery bound were not directly measured.

assertions.summary: The live state is coherent and persistent: intended duplicate-destination routes differ by preference, management is the only default path, and no failed, dynamic, NAT, transient, capture, debug, or abandoned evaluator state was found.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip -4 route show; ip -4 rule show; /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show configuration commands | grep -E 'set protocols (bgp|ospf|rip|isis|babel|pim)|set nat ' || true; systemctl --failed --no-legend --no-pager || true; systemctl is-enabled ssh.service 2>&1 || true; systemctl is-active ssh.service 2>&1 || true; ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep ':22 ' || true; ps -eo pid=,comm=,args= | grep -E '[t]cpdump|[p]ing|[t]race|[d]ebug|[p]robe|[r]oute' || true; find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sort
evidence.observation: Only connected/static data routes and the management default are present; no dynamic protocol or NAT config lines, no failed units, no capture/probe/debug processes, and SSH is listening. Temporary files are normal VyOS state files.

evidence.observation: No duplicate addresses, unexpected data defaults, dynamic-routing services, failed units, capture/debug/probe processes, or temporary files. SSH is listening; persistent route state is in the expected systemd-networkd files.
